Data model overview and module map
Client-facing versus internal cost separation
nodes.rationale: AMPM may earn a margin on vendor and hotel pricing (A-4), so every commercial record stores client-facing amounts and internal cost in separate columns, never one column with a flag; the API uses separate response models per audience so internal cost is never serialised to a client session.

nodes.label: Invoices and payments split by direction
nodes.rationale: Invoices are split by direction rather than dual amount columns: an invoice issued to the client is a client document while invoices received from vendors and hotels are internal cost evidence, closing the leak path noted in audit GP-17; payments carry a direction and counterparty so one table serves receipts, payouts and refunds.

nodes.label: Visibility and access-control model
nodes.rationale: documents.visibility and media_assets.visibility are enumerations (internal/client/guest/public/demo); everything else follows the owning record and the API enforces visibility on every request and on every export.

nodes.label: Demo isolation
nodes.rationale: Demo data lives in the same database, isolated by client_accounts.is_demo, wedding_projects.is_demo and hotels.demo_visible, scoped at the repository layer not in the interface (A-28).

nodes.label: Soft delete and retention
nodes.rationale: Wedding, guest and finance records are never hard-deleted; physical deletion happens only through retention jobs, and AMPM's 26 Oct decision makes deletion require approval, so retention jobs produce proposed deletion lists (A-17, Q8, Q17).

nodes.label: Versioned records and approval locking
nodes.rationale: Versioned records (design/menu/invitation versions, vendor and hotel proposals) are immutable once shared; a new version supersedes the old and approvals point at the exact version_number locked; a new version marks the earlier approval superseded (SPEC §12).

nodes.label: Guest as the atomic record
nodes.rationale: The guest is the atomic record (GP-13); headcounts are counted from guest_function_attendance rows so children and accompanying members are real rows, not a party_count.

nodes.label: Polymorphic references
nodes.rationale: owner_type+owner_id, entity_type+entity_id and record_type+record_id are used only for documents, media, comments, approvals, audit events and notifications, each with a check constraint on the allowed types.

nodes.label: Append-only audit model
nodes.rationale: audit_events records every create, update, delete, approval, share, export and restricted-field read on the guarded entities; rows are append-only and partitioned by month (A-15).

nodes.label: Module entitlement resolution
nodes.rationale: An active or trial subscription grants its plan_modules; an active service_agreement grants its service's module; an active project_members row grants wedding_workspace for that project regardless of subscription state.

nodes.label: Native apps with offline use
nodes.rationale: AMPM's 26 Oct decision (A-1) switched to native iOS and Android apps with offline use from launch; no table changes, the offline change queue is a client-side store mirrored by audit_events on sync.

nodes.label: Assumptions register
nodes.rationale: Each assumption (A-1..A-30) states the draft default and what changes if AMPM decides otherwise; BIZ rule 8 is respected by treating each as a placeholder for AMPM's answer, not a pricing or policy recommendation.

nodes.label: AMPM decisions October 2026
nodes.rationale: AMPM's answers of 25–26 October 2026 recorded in the decision log; §0a lists the ones that change the model: indicative hotel price ranges and street view, pre-pay wedding details, two family representatives, RSVP link scope and self-identification, no automatic deletion, three-month access, live chat, native apps with offline use.

nodes.label: Modelling conventions
nodes.rationale: Every table has a UUID v7 id and standard columns (created/updated/deleted soft delete); money is numeric(14,2) with a currency sibling defaulting to INR; statuses are fixed code enumerations because automation depends on them; timestamps stored in UTC with wedding_projects.timezone driving display.
